attorneys.name: Andrew A. Agard
attorneys.practice_type: Auto Accidents Lawyers in Honolulu, HI
attorneys.bio:
Born and raised in Hawaii, Andrew A. Agard has over 24 years of experience fighting for the legal rights of others. He is a member of the Hawaii Association for Justice (Jury Instruction Review Committee & Amicus Curie Appeals Committee). Hawaii State Bar Association, Public Justice Foundation and American Association for Justice. He also sits on the American Bar Association Advisory Panel and is a long-standing volunteer Arbitrator with the Hawaii Court Annexed Arbitrator Program, also known as CAAP Program and the Native Hawaiian Bar Association.

Andrew's volunteer efforts extend to Volunteer Legal Services Hawaii, a nonprofit organization providing no-charge legal help to the poor and disadvantaged. He is also a volunteer judge for the Hawaii State High School Debate tournaments and a volunteer for various free legal advice clinics.

A graduate of the Kamehameha Schools, Andrew received his Bachelor's Degree from Chaminade University and his Juris Doctorate from the William S. Richardson School of Law.

Outside of work, he is a sports, golf and exercise enthusiast who enjoys coaching beginner baseball, soccer, basketball, tennis and football for kids, fast motorcycles & cars.

Andrew and his wife, Yuri, have two sons, Ikaika and Pono.

attorneys.name: Scott C. Arakaki
attorneys.firm_name: Scott C. Arakaki, Attorney at Law, L.L.L.C.
attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate Litigation Lawyers in Honolulu, HI
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Arakaki is an experienced Hawaii attorney and trial attorney, who litigates on all islands and who helps clients resolve disputes both in and out of court. He concentrates his practice on real estate, commercial, and construction litigation and is experienced with real estate, business, landlord-tenant, administrative, and collection law. Mr. Arakaki has litigated hundreds of cases in state, federal, and/or the appellate courts and has represented numerous clients in private arbitrations, mediation, and administrative agency actions and other legal matters.

Real Estate Litigation And Transactions

Mr. Arakaki has extensive experience with many types of real property matters, including partitions, quiet title actions, foreclosures, contract disputes, real property transactions, specific performance actions, boundary and easement matters, professional negligence, licensing issues, environmental liability, accommodation issues involving Americans with Disabilities Act, commercial leases, and residential landlord-tenant disputes.

Commercial and Construction Litigation And Business Law

Mr. Arakaki is also experienced with contract disputes, shareholder and director disputes, corporate governance, fiduciary duties, construction defect disputes, regulatory disputes, administrative agency matters, formations and dissolutions, asset purchases, buy/sell agreements, and business operations matters.

attorneys.name: Ryan G. S. Au
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Honolulu, HI
attorneys.bio:
Areas of Practice

Business Law. I am proud to represent Hawaii's businesses, whether it is a sole proprietorship or a small or medium sized business in contract disputes, lease disputes, and to collect monies owed to them.

Collection Law. I have successfully recovered monies for persons and businesses where they were owed money based on a contract, lease, promissory note, and for services they had provided to their customers by obtaining judgments and settlements in favor of my clients who are owed monies.

Contract Law. I have represented persons and businesses where they have a contract dispute with another person or business.

Construction Law: Homeowners. I have successfully represented numerous homeowners against licensed contractors who negligently performed their construction work, failed to complete their construction work, failed to obtain the necessary drawings, plans, and building permits, failed to make disclosures required by Hawaii law, and have engaged in unfair and deceptive practices against the homeowner. I have also represented homeowners against unlicensed contractors who perform construction work they are not qualified to preform.

Construction Law: Collections for Contractors. I collect monies for licensed contractors who have not been paid for the proper construction and renovation work they performed.

Personal Injury. I have successfully recovered monies for my clients who have suffered life altering and permanent injuries from automobile accidents, motorcycle accidents, pedestrian accidents, and bicycle accidents through mediation, arbitration, settlement, and at court.

Wrongful Death. The accidental loss of a loved one in a fatal accident is tragic for their family. I have successfully recovered monies for these families where a loved one died as a result of an automobile accident or bicycle accident.

Motor Vehicle Accidents. I have successfully recovered monies for my clients who were injured in car accidents, motorcycle accidents, bicycle accidents, pedestrian accidents, where they received extensive medical care and massage therapy. I have recovered monies to compensate my clients for the medical bills they incurred, and money for their future medical bills, emotional distress, and pain and suffering.

Real Estate Law. I have successfully represented buyers and sellers in disputes related to the purchase of a home and condominium.

Foreclosure Rescue Scams: Homeowner. I have successfully recovered monies for homeowners who were victims of a foreclosure rescue scam. I have represented these homeowners who have lost title to their home to another person or company who had intentionally planned to take title away from the homeowner to make a profit for themselves.

Landlord/Tenant Law: Residential and Commercial Landlords. I have successfully obtained court orders to evict numerous tenants when these tenants fail to pay the rent, breach the lease, or stay beyond the rental period. I have also obtained judgments for landlords for the back owed rent and property damage caused by the tenants.

Landlord/Tenant Law: Commercial Tenants. I have represented commercial tenants in their disputes with their landlords, and have assisted commercial tenants with their leases and assignments of their lease to another tenant.

attorneys.practice_type: Entitlements and Permitting Lawyers in Honolulu, HI
attorneys.bio:
Lisa concentrates her practice in environmental law, land use litigation and commercial litigation.

Her experience includes trials, administrative hearings and appellate work in areas of environmental law, personal injury, contracts and products liability. She is knowledgeable in all phases of litigation practice, from pleading and discovery through injunction, summary judgment, trial, mandamus and appeal.

OUTSIDE THE OFFICE

Lisa devotes her time to volunteering for causes like urban forestry and judicial independence. Currently, she is an officer and director of Smart Trees Pacific, supporting their urban forestry projects, and she serves both as the Hawai‘i Delegate to the American Bar Association and on the board of the American Judicature Society, an independent, nonpartisan, membership organization, working nationally to protect the integrity of the American justice system.

Her devotion to trees also branches into familial territories, as Lisa enjoys researching her family's genealogy.

attorneys.firm_name: Goodsill Anderson Quinn & Stifel A Limited Liability Law Partnership LLP
attorneys.practice_type: Drug And Medical Device Litigation and Medical Malpractice Lawyers in Honolulu, HI
attorneys.bio:
Lindsey is a member of the Business Litigation practice group and focuses her practice on healthcare provider defense in medical liability cases.

Lindsey graduated magna cum laude from Southwestern Law School in Los Angeles, California. During law school, Lindsey participated in the Moot Court Honors Program as an oralist and a writer. She also served as the Senior Lead Articles Editor of the Southwestern Law School Law Review.

Throughout law school and before moving to Hawai'i, Lindsey worked in the litigation department at a full-service law firm in Los Angeles where she handled a variety of civil litigation matters involving insurance defense, premises liability, products liability, and breach of contract.

After practicing for a year in Los Angeles, Lindsey made a lifestyle decision to move to Oahu. Prior to joining Goodsill Anderson Quinn & Stifel A Limited Liability Law Partnership LLP, Lindsey clerked for the Honorable James H. Ashford at First Circuit Court.

attorneys.name: Johnathan C. Bolton
attorneys.firm_name: Goodsill Anderson Quinn & Stifel A Limited Liability Law Partnership LLP
attorneys.practice_type: Bankruptcy and Creditors' Rights Lawyers in Honolulu, HI
attorneys.bio:
Johnathan’s law practice focuses on business and commercial law, real estate and business litigation, debtor/creditor rights, collections, and bankruptcy law. He is licensed to practice law in Hawaii, New York and Texas and is a Solicitor in the United Kingdom. He is the Chair of the firm’s Bankruptcy and Creditors’ Rights practice group and is a member of Goodsill Anderson Quinn & Stifel A Limited Liability Law Partnership LLP's Business Litigation and Real Estate & Insurance Litigation practice groups. He has been board certified in Business Bankruptcy Law for over 15 years and serves on the board that certifies attorneys in bankruptcy and creditors rights law nationwide.

In over 25 years in practice, Johnathan has represented U.S. and international clients in various disputes, ranging from Fortune 500 companies to individuals, in proceedings in State, Federal, Appellate, and Bankruptcy Courts in Hawaii, Guam and on the U.S. Mainland. He also has experience in commercial arbitration proceedings involving investments, contracts, torts and real estate-related claims. He frequently deals with international and cross-border issues.

Clients seek Johnathan for his knowledge, skill and experience in complex, high-stakes situations. He is known for his zealous representation of clients and for finding creative solutions to complex legal problems. He regularly advises and represents local Hawai‘i companies and financial institutions, as well as U.S. mainland and foreign entities conducting business in Hawai‘i and across the Pacific.

attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate Lawyers in Honolulu, HI
attorneys.bio:
Blake W. Bushnell is the founder and managing member of the Bushnell Law Group. Mr. Bushnell has over 35 years of experience representing business and property owners, contractors, subcontractors, design professionals, manufacturers, suppliers, and sureties in a wide variety matters involving construction and real estate, has been involved as the lead attorney for his clients in dispute resolution proceedings before mediators, arbitrators, administrative bodies, and the state and federal courts.

Mr. Bushnell has been selected by his peers for inclusion in the 2023 Edition of The Best Lawyers in America® for his work in construction law and litigation and was also recognized by Honolulu Magazine as one of Hawaii's Best Lawyer’s for 2024 in the areas of construction law and litigation.

Mr. Bushnell has prepared materials and appeared as a panelist at various continuing legal education seminars and has appeared as a speaker before various trade groups . Mr. Bushnell also taught appellate advocacy as an adjunct professor at the William S. Richardson School of Law for several years and serves on a panel of court-appointed arbitrators and mediators for various disputes.

Mr. Bushnell continues to be active in bar and trade association-related activities. He is also currently an active member with the American and Hawaii State Bar Associations and the ABA Forum on the Construction Industry.

attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Honolulu, HI
attorneys.bio:
Jennifer Ching-Agena is admitted to both the Hawai'i State Bar Association and the Washington State Bar Association. She is a Family Law attorney experienced in divorce, post-divorce, custody, child support, and temporary restraining orders. Ms. Ching-Agena is a graduate of Creighton University School of Law.

Ms. Ching-Agena attended Creighton University College of Business Administration and graduated cum laude where she earned her B.S.B.A and majored in International Business and Social Entrepreneurship. She then continued her time in the Midwest and attended Creighton University School of Law where she graduated with her JD. During her time in Law School, she volunteered at Iowa Legal Aid.

Ms. Ching-Agena then moved to Washington State where she volunteered at a Legal Aid society and worked for various Family Law firms and an Insurance Defense firm. The majority of her time spent in Washington State was focused on litigating Family Law matters such as divorce, child custody, child support, and temporary protective orders.

Upon moving back home to Hawai'i, Ms. Ching-Agena joined Greg Ryan & Associates where she zealously advocates for her clients.

attorneys.name: Jennifer F. Chin
attorneys.firm_name: Goodsill Anderson Quinn & Stifel A Limited Liability Law Partnership LLP
attorneys.practice_type: Institutional Financing Lawyers in Honolulu, HI
attorneys.bio:
Jennifer assists clients with resort, commercial, and residential developments, sales and acquisitions of real property, and commercial leasing. She also has experience advising clients on real estate financing, real property tax, and general business matters.

Her experience includes:

Negotiating and drafting transaction documents and advising clients through all aspects of transactions for the acquisition and sale of Hawai‘i real property, including commercial, industrial, resort, golf course, residential, affordable housing, conservation, and agricultural real estate.

Preparing development and sale documents for resort, residential, industrial, and commercial developments.

Preparing condominium and sales documentation and registration of condominium projects with the Hawai‘i Real Estate Commission.

Representing landlords and tenants in connection with ground leases and the leasing of retail shopping center, industrial, office, hotel, golf course, and hospital space.

Preparing and filing subdivision and land sales registrations for residential, affordable housing, commercial, and industrial subdivisions in Hawai’i County, Maui County, and the City and County of Honolulu with the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau and the Hawai‘i Department of Commerce and Consumer Affairs.

Representing borrowers and financial institutions in connection with commercial loans secured by commercial real estate.

Jennifer attended the University of California, Irvine School of Law, where she completed an externship with the Honorable Richard Clifton of the United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit. She also served as a senior editor for the UC Irvine Law Review. Upon graduation from law school, Jennifer worked as a law clerk for the Honorable Gonzalo P. Curiel of the United States District Court for the Southern District of California.

Before entering the legal field, Jennifer worked at the Center for Community Solutions in San Diego, California, a nonprofit agency that provides domestic violence and sexual assault prevention and intervention services.

Outside the Office

Jennifer serves as the firm’s pro bono coordinator and was recognized by Volunteer Legal Services Hawaiʻi with the Kahiau Award in 2023 and by the Hawai‘i Supreme Court Access to Justice Commission with the Outstanding Pro Bono Service Award in 2016 for her policy work with the Hawai‘i Appleseed Center on Law and Economic Justice. She also serves as VicePresident of Board of Directors of Volunteer Legal Services Hawai‘i.

attorneys.practice_type: Motor Vehicle Accidents Lawyers in Honolulu, HI
attorneys.bio:
Rai Saint Chu, born in China, grew up in South Carolina and Pennsylvania, and then attained a BA degree from the University of Maryland and a Juris Doctor degree from the University of Maryland Law School.

Since 1972, Ms. Chu has had a variety of legal and related experiences that enrich her ability to represent her clients. She has worked as a Deputy Public Defender, Legal Aid attorney, lobbyist for the Mental Health Association of Hawaii, attorney for the State House of Representatives, practitioner in various small firms and currently a partner with Turbin Chu, Attorneys primarily a plaintiff's personal injury practice. She has tried over 30 jury trials and hundreds of other legal proceedings in all the Courts and many State agencies in Hawaii.

LEGAL COMMUNITY LEADERSHIP - Rai Saint Chu as the 2009 President of the Hawaii State Bar Association, has served on the boards of the Young Lawyers Division and the Hawaii bar board and chaired the Communications and Public Relations Committee and a member of the Judicial Administration Committee, as well as chairing the 1993 & 2005 HSBA annual fundraisers. She has regularly attended /participated and made presentations in ABA meetings and law programs all over the US and the world, giving her a national perspective on many legal issues, the legal profession, as well as other enriching opportunities.

GOVERNMENT AND COMMUNITY EXPERIENCE - As an elected delegate to the 1978 Hawaii State Constitutional Convention, she was involved in the legal creation of the Judicial Selection Commission, the Intermediate Court of Appeals, Office of Hawaiian Affairs, etc. She was a candidate for State House and elected delegate to several national political conventions. She has also served on the Honolulu Reapportionment Commission, an officer & chair of non profits, such as the Girl Scout Council of Hawaii, Junior League of Honolulu, Punahou Carnival and Planned Parenthood of Hawaii.

He’s won Honolulu Magazine’s “People’s Choice” Award for Best Divorce Lawyer and was later selected as “Best Divorce Lawyer” by Honolulu Weekly Newspaper readers. Additionally, he’s been repeatedly named to the coveted list of Hawaii’s Super Lawyers, an honor given to the top 5% of all Hawaii attorneys.

Outside his courtroom work, Bradley has become a renowned author for his book “Divorce With Dignity” and his affiliate branch by the same name. Bradley also participates in pro bono work as the founder and president of U.S. Arbitration and Mediation of Hawaii and the Pacific, Inc.

attorneys.name: Gail Y. Cosgrove
attorneys.firm_name: Goodsill Anderson Quinn & Stifel A Limited Liability Law Partnership LLP
attorneys.practice_type: Class Actions Lawyers in Honolulu, HI
attorneys.bio:
Gail represents many of Hawaii's major private and public hospitals and medical centers, physicians and other healthcare providers in medical malpractice cases before the Medical Inquiry Conciliation Panel (MICP) and in state and federal courts.

Gail was recognized by Best Lawyers as “Lawyer of the Year” in 2023 for Medical Malpractice Law – Defendants in Honolulu, Hawaii. In January 2024, Gail was lead counsel and obtained a defense verdict for a medical center in a case involving sudden cardiac death of a patient following the patient’s discharge from the medical center. Gail is also an appointed member of the Judicial Arbitration Program which oversees the Court Annexed Arbitration Program.

She practices primarily in civil litigation, medical liability, complex litigation, product liability, and toxic tort litigation.

Gail has represented a domestic building products manufacturer in a multimillion-dollar property damage litigation brought by the State of Hawai‘i and an international architectural firm in a lawsuit for damage sustained to a resort hotel by Hurricane Iniki.

OUTSIDE THE OFFICE

As an active member in the legal community, She is also part of the clinical teaching faculty at the William S. Richardson School of Law.

In the Fall, "Gridiron Gail" emerges and cheers on her favorites - the University of Hawai‘i Rainbow Warriors and Kansas City Chiefs - through rain, sleet, snow, and vog, she is a loyal fan. Gail is also an avid baker and has watched every episode of the Great British Baking Show multiple times! Knitting and crocheting are also favored pastimes with an overly abundant stash of yarn and fiber. Gail is inspired daily by her Chocolate Labrador Belle, to be more doglike - energetic, selfless, resilient, forgiving, loyal and loving.

attorneys.firm_name: Goodsill Anderson Quinn & Stifel A Limited Liability Law Partnership LLP
attorneys.practice_type: Organization and Governance Lawyers in Honolulu, HI
attorneys.bio:
Tanya David is an associate attorney who assists clients from Japan and other countries, as well as domestic clients, in the areas of real estate transactions, corporate matters, and captive insurance law.

During law school, Tanya clerked for the Honorable Judge Garret Wong of the San Francisco Superior Court. In 2019, she attended Waseda Law School in Tokyo, Japan. Tanya received her Bachelor of Sciences degree from Syracuse University with honors and her law degree from University of California Hastings College of the Law. While at Hastings, Tanya served as a member of the American Constitutional Society, Hastings Hawai'i Hui, and the Women's Law Society. She also served as the editor for the Hastings Constitutional Law Quarterly Journal.

OUTSIDE THE OFFICE

Tanya was born in Tokyo and moved to Hawai'i at the age of four. Despite moving away at such a young age, she retained her reading, writing and speaking abilities through concentrated Japanese language studies and frequent visits to Japan to study and work. In her free time, Tanya enjoys surfing, hiking and spending time with her dogs at the beach.

PERSONAL HAWAII QUOTE

Growing up in Hawai'i is an incredibly unique experience where we as a community are defined by our multicultural backgrounds-all of which enrich our lives and create a robust sense of pride and Aloha.

attorneys.bio:
Deborah DiCristofaro concentrates her practice in civil litigation. Prior to joining Goodsill Anderson Quinn & Stifel A Limited Liability Law Partnership LLP, she served two terms clerking for Magistrate Judge Wes Reber Porter of the United States District Court, District of Hawai‘i.

Deborah was born and raised in Connecticut and received her Juris Doctor from the University of Connecticut School of Law. While in law school, she served as an Articles Editor for the Connecticut Law Review, Vice President of the UConn Mock Trial Society, and was an active Member of the Connecticut Moot Court Board. Deborah was also a judicial extern for Justice Michael D. Prior to practicing law, Deborah was an AmeriCorps VISTA at the Kumuhonua Transitional Living Center in Kapolei where she worked to help homeless residents secure permanent housing.

In her free time, Deborah enjoys staying active by surfing, traveling, and hiking with her dog.

attorneys.name: P. Gregory Frey
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce with Decency Lawyers in Honolulu, HI
attorneys.bio:
P. Gregory Frey, JD4386, known to all simply as "Greg," is a third generation attorney, following in the footsteps of his paternal grandfather (USC Law) and father (Stanford Law). He quite literally grew-up, together with his twin brother, under his Father's desk -- the very desk he proudly sits at today, decades later. Greg defines himself as a "old school attorney," and he's proud of that reality. His father ----- a rather famed "3-dot" attorney member of the Hawaii State Bar way "back-in-the-day" ----- instilled in him day-after-day that good attorneys, great attorneys do more than simply represent their clients, they "go to the mat" for each of them, and along the way, volunteer often to help those in need and also try to do good things in the community, for the community. Greg took the advice to heart, and as a result, his personal life clearly demonstrates that he's got an amazing philanthropic spirit & energy & devotion which rivals most. In a few words, Greg has "given back" for decades, for his entire career. Here's but a few of the things he's done which are important to him, and for which he has ALWAYS carried a sincere passion & special devotion:

** Service on the Hawaii State Bar Association Board for about 10 years, culminating as Bar President in 2020 (arguably the most prestigious philanthropic honor a lawyer can achieve in his/her career).

** Service on literally dozens (if not hundreds) of Committees in Family Court of the First Circuit (Oahu) spanning over 30 years, to include appointment by the Chief Justice of the Hawaii Supreme Court to Special Master positions in divorce & paternity cases, and extensive volunteer work with the Access to Justice program in Family Court, Volunteer Legal Services of Hawaii ("VLSH") and Mediation Center of the Pacific ("MCP").

** Service on numerous local school boards, to include Saint Louis School Trustees for about 12 years and Sacred Hearts Academy for some 6 years.

** Service on numerous Alumni Association boards, to include St. Louis Alumni Assoc. for 17 years (to include 10 consecutive years as President) and Santa Clara University Alumni for about 3 years (travelling from HI to CA for each meeting in the days before Zoom).

** Service on the Waikiki Yacht Club ("WYC") Board of Directors for about 9 years, culminating as Commodore in 1997 ("fun fact" - Greg was the first son of a former commodore to also be elected commodore in the famed Club's almost 80 year existence).

** Service on the ABRACADABRA 2000 National Board for years, the syndicate responsible for getting the first boat out of HAWAII to enter the famed AMERICA's CUP.

** Member & Partner & Managing Attorney of Coates Frey & Hackett, AAL LLLC for 22 years (from 1996-2018) & now, Member & Partner & Senior Attorney of Coates Frey & Hackett, AAL LLLC).

** Founder & Bd. President of SeMPer FREY, Inc., dba The Wishes GRANTed Foundation, a 501(c)(3) tax-exempt Public Charity established to honor his (twin) brother, LtCol. Grant V. Frey, USMC (Ret.) who was tragically lost to COVID-19 in 2020.

** Co-owner of The P.I.A.E Group, LLC dba The Pacific Ink & Art Expo aka Hawaii Tattoo Expo.

All this volunteer service & hard work to try to help & to guide others has led Greg to enjoy & to earn & to achieve lots of accolades, honors & recognition, to include these:

** Two-time recipient of VLSH's Kahiau Award.

** Inducted to SLS's Gallery of Distinguished Achievers ("GODA'), 2018.

** Lifetime appointment as SLS' Trustee Emeritus.

** Inductee to Santa Clara Rugby Hall of Fame, 2018.

** WYC Member of the Year, 1997.

If asked, Greg will tell you & anyone who will listen that each of these "life experiences" & related honors / recognition has allowed him to create and maintain a very special understanding of the unique needs of local folks, and how to best meet these needs. Greg's a true "people person" who is devoted to "talk story" with his clients until solutions are found, and until work gets done to the total satisfaction (hopefully!?!) of each person Greg works for and works with. His "jump right in" approach to his work as a Family Law attorney comes from all the unique & hands-on stuff he has done for decades. As said, Greg sees himself as a "local boy who helps local folks." Please allow Greg to help YOU when & if needed.

** Service on literally dozens (if not hundreds) of Committees in Family Court of the First Circuit (Oahu) spanning over 30 years, to include appointment by the Chief Justice of the Hawaii Supreme Court to Special Master positions in divorce & paternity cases, and extensive volunteer work with the Access to Justice program in Family Court, Volunteer Legal Services of Hawaii ("VLSH") and Mediation Center of the Pacific ("MCP").

** Service on numerous local school boards, to include Saint Louis School Trustees for about 12 years and Sacred Hearts Academy for some 6 years.

** Service on numerous Alumni Association boards, to include St. Louis Alumni Assoc. for 17 years (to include 10 consecutive years as President) and Santa Clara University Alumni for about 3 years (travelling from HI to CA for each meeting in the days before Zoom).

** Service on the Waikiki Yacht Club ("WYC") Board of Directors for about 9 years, culminating as Commodore in 1997 ("fun fact" - Greg was the first son of a former commodore to also be elected commodore in the famed Club's almost 80 year existence).

** Service on the ABRACADABRA 2000 National Board for years, the syndicate responsible for getting the first boat out of HAWAII to enter the famed AMERICA's CUP.

** Member & Partner & Managing Attorney of Coates Frey & Hackett, AAL LLLC for 22 years (from 1996-2018) & now, Member & Partner & Senior Attorney of Coates Frey & Hackett, AAL LLLC).

** Founder & Bd. President of SeMPer FREY, Inc., dba The Wishes GRANTed Foundation, a 501(c)(3) tax-exempt Public Charity established to honor his (twin) brother, LtCol. Grant V. Frey, USMC (Ret.) who was tragically lost to COVID-19 in 2020.

** Co-owner of The P.I.A.E Group, LLC dba The Pacific Ink & Art Expo aka Hawaii Tattoo Expo.

All this volunteer service & hard work to try to help & to guide others has led Greg to enjoy & to earn & to achieve lots of accolades, honors & recognition, to include these:

** Two-time recipient of VLSH's Kahiau Award.

** Inducted to SLS's Gallery of Distinguished Achievers ("GODA'), 2018.

** Lifetime appointment as SLS' Trustee Emeritus.

** Inductee to Santa Clara Rugby Hall of Fame, 2018.

** WYC Member of the Year, 1997.

If asked, Greg will tell you & anyone who will listen that each of these "life experiences" & related honors / recognition has allowed him to create and maintain a very special understanding of the unique needs of local folks, and how to best meet these needs. Greg's a true "people person" who is devoted to "talk story" with his clients until solutions are found, and until work gets done to the total satisfaction (hopefully!?!) of each person Greg works for and works with. His "jump right in" approach to his work as a Family Law attorney comes from all the unique & hands-on stuff he has done for decades. As said, Greg sees himself as a "local boy who helps local folks." Please allow Greg to help YOU when & if needed.

attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate Development Lawyers in Honolulu, HI
attorneys.bio:
If you're looking for help understanding the intricacies of international business, look no further than Alan.

Alan handles "whatever the Japanese get involved in". He has experience in assisting Japanese companies and individual investors and other Asia-based and foreign clients in real estate and commercial transactions (e.g., commercial real estate, golf courses, hotels, business sales and acquisitions), mergers and acquisitions, financing transactions, corporate and other business matters. He also handles administrative matters such as licensing applications for insurance companies, including captive insurers, liquor license and franchise registrations. In addition, Alan has often been sought for his assistance with business visa applications for foreign clients.

After graduating from law school, Alan served as law clerk to the late Honorable Yoshimi Hayashi of the Hawai‘i Supreme Court.

OUTSIDE THE OFFICE

Born and raised in Japan, Alan reads, writes and speaks fluent Japanese. He is also knowledgeable in Japanese cultural and business practices. Alan is a sports enthusiast and has attended a Super Bowl, a Sugar Bowl, an NBA Finals game, the U.S. Open Golf Tournament and countless Major League Baseball games among other sporting events. He loves to travel and has visited 30 countries on 6 different continents to date. In his spare time Alan enjoys going to movies and listening to J-Pop and K-Pop music.

Throughout his career, Andrew has focused almost exclusively on representing consumers, and he has witnessed first-hand the impact that companies can have when they treat consumers in an abusive manner or refuse to fix their mistakes. Andrew is committed to using federal consumer protection laws to level the playing field between individuals and companies.

Andrew has significant experience in the consumer law field. Since 2011, Andrew has litigated over 350 cases in federal courts, including more than 100 cases against each of the “Big 3” credit reporting agencies and dozens of cases against internet lenders who prey on financially vulnerable consumers. In many of these cases, Andrew was the primary or co-author on dozens of briefs leading to favorable, published decisions on behalf of his clients. For example, along with Ms. Kelly, Andrew drafted the opposition to the motion to dismiss in Williams v. Big Picture Loans, LLC, which resulted in the first decision from a federal court finding that an online tribal lender could be sued by Virginia consumers in federal court.

Andrew is licensed and primarily practices in Virginia and Hawai‘i but has litigated cases across the country, including in Maryland, the District of Columbia, California, Florida, Pennsylvania, Arizona, Texas, New Jersey, and New York. He has been repeatedly recognized as a Rising Star by Super Lawyers Magazine, and is also a regular speaker at local and national conferences on consumer litigation matters, including on issues related to credit reporting, class actions, arbitration, and payday loans.

Outside the office, Andrew enjoys spending time with his family and trying to lower his single-digit handicap.

attorneys.practice_type: Commercial Litigation Lawyers in Honolulu, HI
attorneys.bio:
Bryan Harada concentrates his practice in the areas of civil litigation, trusts & estates litigation, and intellectual property matters. He has extensive experience in assisting clients understand their rights, duties, and obligations in order to allow them to make informed decisions.

Examples of his work include:

Civil Litigation: Represented plaintiffs and defendants in a variety of matters, including but not limited to the following: personal injury claims, motor vehicle injury and wrongful death claims, SCUBA wrongful death claims, sexual abuse/assault civil claims, partition actions, commercial foreclosure claims, and breach of contract actions.

Trusts & Estates Litigation: Represented petitioners, respondents, and interested parties in a variety of contested actions involving claims for trustee removal and surcharge, demands for accountings, personal representative mismanagement, and appointment of guardians.

Arbitration: Represented parties in contested disputes regarding business contracts to reach favorable settlements.

Mediation: Represented parties in a variety of civil matters to reach favorable settlements.

Intellectual Property: Represented and advised clients with federal and state trademark registrations, copyright registrations, copyright infringement issues, trademark infringement issues, publicity rights issues, and other intellectual property matters.

Bryan was born and raised in Hawaii, attended Punahou, and went away to college on the mainland. After returning to Hawaii and graduating from law school, he served as law clerk to the Honorable Rhonda A. Nishimura (ret.), and then gained valuable experience as an associate at two intellectual property boutique firms and one general service firm. He also served as a session attorney for Representative (now Senator) Karl Rhoads of the Hawaii House of Representatives during the 2014 session.

attorneys.firm_name: Goodsill Anderson Quinn & Stifel A Limited Liability Law Partnership LLP
attorneys.practice_type: Business Litigation Lawyers in Honolulu, HI
attorneys.bio:
Sara M.K.Y. Hayden is an associate in the firm’s business litigation department.

Sara received her J.D. from the University of Hawai‘i William S. Richardson School of Law. During law school, Sara served as a Senior Editor for the Asian-Pacific Law and Policy Journal, as a member of Phi Delta Phi, and as a William S. Richardson School of Law Student Ambassador. She received the CALI Excellence for the Future Award for Children, Parents & the Law. Her Second-Year Seminar paper, entitled “Electing the Bench: An Analysis of the Possible Negative Effects of Judicial Elections on Hawaiʻi’s Legal Community,” won the law school’s 2017 Best Overall Second Year Seminar Paper Award and was published in Volume 18, Issue 1, of the Asian-Pacific Law and Policy Journal.

Following law school, Sara clerked for the Honorable Karen T. Nakasone on the criminal calendar and for the Honorable Gary W.B. Chang on the civil calendar at the Circuit Court of the First Circuit. Sara also clerked for Judge Nakasone following her appointment as Associate Judge at the Intermediate Court of Appeals.

Following her clerkships, Sara worked as an associate at another law firm, and practiced in the areas of complex civil litigation, insurance defense, construction litigation, and commercial litigation.

OUTSIDE THE OFFICE

Sara enjoys reading, shopping, and spending time outdoors with her husband, two young daughters, and their dog.

Ms. Heidt earned her Juris Doctorate degree from the University of Denver School of Law in 1998 and was admitted to the Indiana Bar in 1998 and the Hawaii Bar in 2008. Ms. Heidt is also an active member of the Hawaii State Bar Association.

In 1998 Ms. Heidt began working for Yosha Krahulik & Levy law firm in Indianapolis, Indiana where she gained experience in personal injury and medical malpractice law. She enjoys sailing, boogie boarding, hiking, reading and swimming. She is married and is the proud mother of three boys.

attorneys.name: David J. Hoftiezer
attorneys.firm_name: Goodsill Anderson Quinn & Stifel A Limited Liability Law Partnership LLP
attorneys.practice_type: Aviation Lawyers in Honolulu, HI
attorneys.bio:
David J. Hoftiezer is a litigator who concentrates his practice on aviation, professional liability defense, personal injury and premises liability, corporate disputes, and environmental law. David also has experience representing corporate and individual clients in internal investigations, including matters involving the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act, the False Claims Act, and securities and accounting fraud.

David began his legal career as an associate at Hughes Hubbard & Reed LLP in Washington, D.C. as a member of the firm’s Securities Litigation and Anti-Corruption and Internal Investigations practice groups. He moved to Hawai‘i with his family in 2013, joined Goodsill Anderson Quinn & Stifel A Limited Liability Law Partnership LLPs litigation team, and became a partner at Goodsill Anderson Quinn & Stifel A Limited Liability Law Partnership LLP in 2018. David is Co-Chair of Goodsill Anderson Quinn & Stifel A Limited Liability Law Partnership LLPs Professional Development Committee and a member of Goodsill Anderson Quinn & Stifel A Limited Liability Law Partnership LLPs Technology and Hiring & Recruiting Committees. When he is not working or spending time with his wife and daughter, David volunteers and serves as a board member of the Honolulu Theater for Youth and Volunteer Legal Services of Hawai‘i.

David grew up in small-town Wisconsin before attending Dartmouth College in New Hampshire. He worked for several years before attending University of California Davis School of Law, where David served as a Senior Articles Editor on the Law Review and was a member of the Moot Court Board. Prior to law school, David worked as Director of Dartmouth College’s Rahr Geography lab, where he taught Geographical Information Systems and Remote Sensing labs for Dartmouth College’s Geography and Environmental Studies departments.

attorneys.name: Ted H.S. Hong
attorneys.firm_name: Ted H.S. Hong Attorney at Law, LLLC
attorneys.practice_type: Administrative Law Lawyers in Hilo, HI
attorneys.bio:
Ted has lived in Hilo in 1991. He has been married for 32 years to Terri Lum. He has two adult children, Katharine (26), living in Los Angeles and Noah (24), finishing his degree at UH-Hilo.

Ted is in private practice concentrating in employment, workplace law and civil litigation. He is an experienced litigator with real world experience as lead counsel in more than twenty-six (26) jury trials in State and Federal Court. He has represented clients before the appellate courts of the State of Hawaii and the federal Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals. He has been lead counsel in over fifty (50) arbitrations and a similar number of mediations.

Ted has served as the Chief Labor Negotiator for the State of Hawaii during the Lingle Administration. He was interim Regent for the University of Hawaii. He served as Corporation Counsel and Assistant Corporation Counsel under the Yamashiro Administration.

Ted recently authored a law review article, Masterpiece Cakeshop: "Does Anybody Really Know What Time It Is?" 52 UIC J. Marshall L. Rev. 83 (2018). Ted was lead counsel in what has been recognized as a ground breaking decision in the defamation case, Nakamoto v. Kawauchi, 142 Hawaii 259, 270, 418 P.3d 600, 611 (2018), which redefined the torts of defamation and negligent investigation in the State of Hawaii.

Ted is active in our community. He recently served as the Chairperson for the Hilo Yacht 100th Anniversary; Chairman for the Boy Scout Makahiki; Chair for the 100th Anniversary of Scouting on the Big Island; Chairperson for Friends of Scouting Community Fundraising, and was District Chair for Boy Scouts of America for Puna, Kau and Hilo. He was the Cubmaster for the Hilo Hongwanji Cub Scout Pack 23. He was a member of the Rotary Club of South Hilo. He was a member of the Hilo Medical Center Foundation. He has been a member of Hilo Intermediate School SCC and the Kaumana Elementary School's Safety and Audit Committees.

attorneys.firm_name: Goodsill Anderson Quinn & Stifel A Limited Liability Law Partnership LLP
attorneys.practice_type: Construction Law Lawyers in Honolulu, HI
attorneys.bio:
Forest is a partner and a member of the Business Litigation practice group at Goodsill Anderson Quinn & Stifel A Limited Liability Law Partnership LLP, and has experience in business and commercial litigation, construction litigation, insurance defense litigation, retail litigation, and condominium association law.

Forest earned his J.D. degree from the University of Iowa, College of Law, where he was awarded the Dean’s Award for finishing top of his class for Constitutional Law. While attending the University of Iowa, Forest externed for the U.S. District Court, District of Oregon for Magistrate Judge Paul Papak.

Forest began his career as a Hawaii state prosecutor assigned to felony cases and had the opportunity to serve as lead trial attorney in over fifteen jury trials. Forest has also tried multiple civil jury trials and bench trials as well in Hawaii. After leaving the prosecutor’s office, he went on to become a member of an in-house legal team for a California based construction company.

Prior to joining Goodsill Anderson Quinn & Stifel A Limited Liability Law Partnership LLP, Forest practiced for three years with a mid-sized law firm in Honolulu focusing on commercial and construction litigation. Forest has been with Goodsill Anderson Quinn & Stifel A Limited Liability Law Partnership LLP since 2019 and examples of his work include:

Construction Litigation: Defended commercial and residential contractors and developers in multi-million dollar lawsuits pertaining to alleged constructions defects.

Professional Malpractice: Defended real estate agents, attorneys, accountants and other professionals in malpractice lawsuits.

Insurance Defense and Coverage Litigation: Regularly defends insureds against a wide array of tort and contract claims. Defended insureds in premise liability lawsuits, general liability lawsuits, and automobile accidents. He has also litigated first and third-party bad faith lawsuits.

Premise Liability: Litigated numerous premise liability cases through arbitration and trial related to alleged incidents that have occurred in large box stores, hotels, and other retail properties throughout Hawaii.

Employment Related Litigation: Litigated numerous lawsuits defending a company’s non-compete/nonsolicitation agreements and other employment related matters.

Condominium Association Law: Represented numerous condominium associations in disputes with companies, vendors, and developers throughout Hawaii. Also, serves a general counsel for condominium associations across the State of Hawaii.

attorneys.practice_type: Organization and Governance Lawyers in Honolulu, HI
attorneys.bio:
Peter is the former managing partner of the firm. He focuses his practice in the areas of real estate transactions, business and commercial transactions, corporate documentation and immigration issues.

Peter makes good things happen for his clients. He has represented a major Hawai‘i hotel owner in a spin-off of one of its full-service hotels; acted as co-counsel in representing a seller in closing the sale of a full-service hotel in Sydney, Australia; and acted as co-counsel in representing a borrower in closing $1.8 billion worth of CMBS (commercial mortgage-backed securities) and conventional mortgage loans, secured by full-service hotels in Hawai‘i and California.

We know Peter is one of the top lawyers in Hawai‘i. But don't take our word for it: since 1995, Peter has been recognized by colleagues for inclusion in The Best Lawyers in America© for practicing immigration law in Hawai‘i.

OUTSIDE THE OFFICE

For over three decades, Peter has been a dedicated leader in his community. He's a member and former president of the Hawai‘i Chapter of the American Immigration Lawyers Association, director of the board of Honpa Hongwanji Hawai‘i Betsuin, and vice president and director of the board for the Honolulu Police Community Foundation.

Don't forget to ask Peter about his golf game-he's a member of the Oahu Country Club.

attorneys.name: Jonathan A. Kobayashi
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Honolulu, HI
attorneys.bio:
Born and raised in Honolulu, Mr. Kobayashi received his Bachelor of Art degree in Business and Administrative Studies from Lewis & Clark College in Portland, Oregon and his Juris Doctor degree from Seattle University School of Law.

In 1995, Mr. Kobayashi started his practice with the Honolulu law firm of Kobayashi, Sugita & Goda. In 2007, then a partner with the firm handling complex commercial litigation and construction litigation matters, Mr. Kobayashi left the island and his practice to serve as General Manager for hotel and restaurant in Washington state’s Orcas Island. There he was responsible for all aspects of the day-to-day business operations for both the transient accommodations and the food & beverage/catering services.

Additionally, he handled all short and long term financial and organizational planning, marketing, communications, human resources, business development, contract negotiations, drafting and administration, payroll and corporate filings.

In 2014, Mr. Kobayashi returned to Honolulu to serve as President and CEO of Ahahui Koa Anuenue, a designated fundraising non-profit corporation supporting the University of Hawaii Athletic Department, responsible for raising over six million dollars annually through premium ticket and parking sales and booster club contributions.

In 2017, Mr. Kobayashi returned to his law practice with Kobayashi Sugita & Goda, initially as an Of Counsel and eventually as partner, where he resumed his focus on commercial litigation.

In 2024, Mr. Kobayashi decided to shift the focus of his law practice and joined Greg Ryan & Associates where he now handles all aspects of family law. He is an experienced and skilled litigator and an effective agent for resolution, whether advocating on your behalf, or working collaboratively with both parties towards a mediated agreement.

attorneys.practice_type: Appeals Lawyers in Honolulu, HI
attorneys.bio:
Geoffrey K.S. Komeya has been a lawyer for thirty years and joined the firm in 1996. He received his law degree from the William S. Richardson School of Law at the University of Hawaii, where he was the Editor-in-Chief of the Law Review, a member of the National Environmental Moot Court Team, received several American Jurisprudence Awards for excellence in Tort Law, Insurance Law, Negotiation, Mediation, Alternative Dispute Resolution, Appellate Advocacy, and Federal Taxation, and co-authored a law review article on Tort law in Hawaii published in 1992. After graduating from law school, Mr. Komeya served as a law clerk to Federal District Judge Samuel P. King of the United States District Court for the District of Hawaii for one year, and to Chief Justice Ronald T.Y. Moon of the Supreme Court of Hawaii for two years. Mr. Komeya has participated in the successful prosecution of the firm's largest cases and his practice often focuses on difficult and/or complex cases in the medical malpractice, products liability, personal injury, motor vehicle, toxic/environmental, insurance, consumer fraud/unfair and deceptive trade practices, construction/industrial, appeals, and aviation areas. Mr. Komeya is also a member of the Supreme Court of Hawaii's Standing Committee on the Hawaii Rules of Appellate Procedure. Mr. Komeya has been named to the Best Lawyers in Hawai`i in the fields of Personal Injury Litigation - Plaintiffs, Medical Malpractice Law - Plaintiffs, Products Liability Litigation - Plaintiffs, Insurance Law, Litigation - Insurance, and Mass Tort Litigation/Class Actions - Plaintiffs, and has received the highest peer and client ratings of "AV" from the Martindale-Hubbell Attorney Rating System.

attorneys.practice_type: Construction Litigation Lawyers in Honolulu, HI
attorneys.bio:
Adrian Lavarias joined the firm as an associate in 2006. Mr. Lavarias' areas of practice include construction litigation, personal injury litigation, real estate litigation, trusts and estates litigation, and commercial litigation.

Mr. Lavarias graduated summa cum laude from the William S. Richardson School of Law. During law school, he worked as a summer associate with the firm. He also worked as an extern to the Honorable Susan Oki Mollway of the United States District Court for the District of Hawaii, the Honorable Michael D. Wilson of the First Circuit Court, State of Hawaii, and the University of Hawaii General Counsel's office. Mr. Lavarias has also served as a member and casenotes editor of the University of Hawaii's Law Review and a member of the Delta Theta Phi legal fraternity.

Mr. Lavarias is a graduate of the University of Hawaii at Manoa's College of Business Administration, where he obtained a degree in Finance. During his undergraduate studies, Mr. Lavarias worked as a student assistant to the Athletics Director at the University of Hawaii.

Construction Litigation

Represented subcontractor in mechanics' lien action involving the recovery of $3 million. A lien was successfully attached and proceedings to recover the amounts have commenced.

Represented general contractor in recovery of damages from State of Hawaii stemming from project delays and inadequate project designs. Case settled out of Court.

Represented mechanical design contractor against defective design claims brought by homeowner's association. Case was settled following a mini trial in the first Circuit Court. Mini trial jury returned defense verdict in favor of mechanical contractor.

Represented Engineer in professional negligence claims on Maui. Case was settled out of court prior to trial.

Represented contractors in various administrative proceedings before the State's Regulated Industries Complaints Office.

Personal Injury Litigation

Represented landowner against claims brought by minor and family of minor for injuries allegedly sustained when minor was assaulted by third party on landowner's property. Case settled out of court favorably for landowner.

Represented general contractor in claims brought against homeowners for defamation and injury to business reputation. Homeowner's insurance company paid $1 million to settle case.

Represented employer against defamation claims brought by former employee in connection with employee's termination. Case was settled before trial favorably for employer.

Real Estate Litigation

Represented prominent Hawaii Church against claims brought by Native Hawaiian activist for alleged violation of Hawaii's environmental protection laws, Hawaii's Native Hawaiian burial laws (HRS Chapter 6E). attorneys.bio:
Due to his passion to protect the rights of the residents throughout Hawaii, Attorney James T. Leavitt founded Leavitt, Yamane & Soldner more than 30 years ago. Prior to becoming a personal injury lawyer, Attorney Leavitt attended University of Michigan Law School where he earned his Juris Doctorate in 1966. He first arrived to Hawaii as a United States Marine Corps Judge Advocate General and was assigned to the 14th Naval District in Pearl Harbor.

During his time in the service, Attorney Leavitt made friends with Hawaiian natives and civilians. When he was offered a position at the Hawaii Public Defenders Office, he gladly accepted the offer. Since then, he has practiced law in the state of Hawaii for over four decades. He is committed to an excellent work ethic and is relentless in pursuing maximum compensation on behalf of his clients. No matter what that case is, he stands by his clients from the moment he takes their case to the second they are able to recover compensation. When you need aggressive representation, contact Attorney Leavitt.

attorneys.name: Judy Y. Lee
attorneys.firm_name: Goodsill Anderson Quinn & Stifel A Limited Liability Law Partnership LLP
attorneys.practice_type: Trust and Estate Litigation and Controversy Lawyers in Honolulu, HI
attorneys.bio:
Judy Yuriko Lee concentrates her practice in estate planning, probate, guardianship and trust administration. She has represented clients in establishing wills and trusts, implementing sophisticated estate planning techniques, administering and terminating trust estates and resolving controversies concerning estate administration issues. She has been awarded an AV rating by Martindale-Hubbell Law Directory, and has been recognized with a listing in The Best Lawyers in America since the 2006 edition. Judy is recognized in Chambers & Partners Private Wealth Law-Hawaii as a Band 1 ranked attorney. Judy has been elected to the prestigious American College of Trust and Estate Counsel ("ACTEC") and is currently serving as the Hawaii State Chair of ACTEC.

Examples of her work include:

Trust Administration: Represented individual and corporate trustees in administering and terminating trust estates.

Estate Litigation: Represented beneficiaries in will contest proceeding and negotiated settlement and resolution of issues in contested trust matters.

Estate Planning: Prepared numerous wills, revocable and irrevocable trusts, powers of attorney, gifting and transfer instruments.

Probate: Represented individual and corporate personal representatives of both local decedents and non-resident alien decedents.

Conservatorship/Guardianship: Represented clients to establish and administer conservatorships and guardianships of minors and incapacitated adults.

Partnership and Corporate Planning: Established partnerships, limited liability companies and corporations and prepared documents on the administration of such entities.

Judy is an active participant of the estate planning community. She is the past Chair of the Probate and Estate Planning Section of the Hawaii State Bar and is a frequent speaker for the continuing legal education programs and other professional and community associations. Judy has served as an adjunct professor at the University of Hawai‘i School of Law, teaching trusts and estates, and federal income tax, and has published several articles on trusts and estates topics. Born and raised in Hawai‘i, she enjoys family and church activities during her leisure time.

OUTSIDE THE OFFICE

Frequent speaker at the Hawai‘i Tax Institute and other continuing legal education programs, as well as adjunct professor at University of Hawai‘i William S. Richardson School of Law, Judy still manages to find time to participate in church activities and travel with family.

attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate, Land Use & Hospitality Lawyers in Hilo, HI
attorneys.bio:
Steve Lim is the Administrative Partner of the firm's Hilo office and is headquartered in the firm's Honolulu office. He has over twenty years experience on the Big Island, Maui, Kauai, and Oahu in all phases of the real property development process. Mr. Lim concentrates in advising clients on real property due diligence reviews, land use entitlements and administrative issues, including litigation of land use and real property disputes. In 2014, The Best Lawyers in America selected Mr. Lim as Lawyer of the Year (Hawai‘i)—Real Estate Law (Land Use & Zoning Law).

Representative Matters

Real Property Acquisition, Development, and Sale Represents developers and major land owners in all phases of project development. Performs due diligence on complex real estate purchases, including pre-closing review of title issues and zoning and permit compliance, as well as proposed use reviews. Work involves land use entitlements and registration of subdivisions and condominiums, and advising clients on licensing and permitting requirements at the federal, state and local levels. Represents individuals and development entities in the purchase and sale of real property, and in actions to quiet title.

Resort, Master Planned Community and Golf Course Development Assists owners and developers with multi-phased resort and golf course development projects. Obtains state and county zoning entitlements, and advises clients on real property, construction and related areas of the law.

Licenses, Permits & Administrative Appeals Assists clients in obtaining a wide variety of licenses and permits from governmental agencies, including liquor licenses, conditional use permits, industrial wastewater discharge permits, shoreline setback variances, site plan review permits, and special management area use permits, among others. Obtains approvals for variances from affordable housing rules, and zoning and subdivision requirements. Represents clients in litigation of administrative appeals before agencies, boards, and the courts.

attorneys.firm_name: Goodsill Anderson Quinn & Stifel A Limited Liability Law Partnership LLP
attorneys.practice_type: Class Actions Lawyers in Honolulu, HI
attorneys.bio:
Stacy counsels clients on a broad range of civil disputes, with a particular focus on premises liability and personal injury defense for Hawaii’s retail, hospitality and tourism industry. She has also represented developers, general contractors, subcontractors and architects in various construction defect and design matters. She has litigated a wide range of cases for Hawaii, national and internationally-based clients in Hawaii’s federal and state courts, and before Hawaii administrative law panels. Stacy serves on Goodsill Anderson Quinn & Stifel A Limited Liability Law Partnership LLPs Hiring, Summer Associate and Wellness committees.

Prior to returning home to Oahu and joining Goodsill Anderson Quinn & Stifel A Limited Liability Law Partnership LLP in 2015, Stacy was a litigation associate at Schulte Roth & Zabel LLP in New York City, where her practice focused on complex litigation, including securities class actions, shareholder derivative and commercial matters. Stacy also represented corporate and individual clients in regulatory investigations and enforcement actions. While at Schulte, she was a member of its Summer Associate recruiting committee and oversaw training of the Summer Associate mock trial programs.

OUTSIDE THE OFFICE

Stacy is not only a top litigator, she’s also a top chef who knows a thing or two about making homemade pastas and ice cream. When she’s not experimenting in the kitchen, she enjoys spending time with her husband, two young sons and golden retriever (preferably on the beach).

attorneys.name: Deirdre Marie
attorneys.firm_name: Goodsill Anderson Quinn & Stifel A Limited Liability Law Partnership LLP
attorneys.practice_type: Appellate Practice Lawyers in Honolulu, HI
attorneys.bio:
Deirdre Marie-Iha is an appellate practitioner, appellate consultant, and civil litigator. Her appellate experience is extensive and spans more than 20 years in both federal and state court. She has argued numerous times before the Hawaiʻi Supreme Court, the Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals, and the Hawaiʻi Intermediate Court of Appeals. Deirdre has personally handled well over a hundred appellate proceedings as lead appellate counsel, and has consulted on hundreds more. Over the years, Deirdre’s appellate caseload has generated more than 40 published opinions in the state and federal appellate courts. Her current appellate work includes corporate governance, business matters, banking, and trust litigation. She also routinely handles complex civil matters in the trial courts, particularly business disputes and trust disputes.

In her appellate consulting practice, Deirdre advises existing teams of attorneys or solo practitioners on anticipated appellate issues and appellate procedure in the Hawaiʻi state appellate courts. Appellate consulting is a flexible, collaborative concept that adjusts easily to the needs of the client and the existing team of attorneys. It can range anywhere from assisting solo practitioners who are unfamiliar with the appellate process to collaborating with large groups of attorneys who are representing sophisticated national businesses. Appellate consulting can start as early as a proceeding begins in the trial court, especially when a novel legal issue might impact a case of substantial potential exposure. It can also start after the entry of judgment in trial court but before post-judgment motions are litigated. And appellate consulting can start anytime during the appellate process, including during certiorari or transfer proceedings at the Hawaiʻi Supreme Court, or in offering assistance in preparing for appellate oral argument.

Before joining Goodsill Anderson Quinn & Stifel A Limited Liability Law Partnership LLP in 2018, Deirdre practiced for 14 years as a deputy attorney general at the Hawaiʻi AG’s office, where she handled a number of high-profile, high-stakes matters, in both trial court and on appeal. This included the furloughs during the 2008-2009 financial crisis; the enactment and subsequent defense of the Marriage Equality Act in 2013-2015; successfully defending against constitutional challenges to the State’s election and campaign finance laws; and complex litigation regarding the State’s retiree health benefits.

Deirdre has been practicing for more than 25 years. In 2003-2004, Deirdre clerked for the Honorable Corinne K. A. Watanabe, Associate Judge of the Hawaiʻi Intermediate Court of Appeals (now retired). Before that, Deirdre practiced in California. She graduated from the University of Colorado School of Law in 1999. Her undergraduate degree is in History, from Cornell University, where she graduated Phi Beta Kappa.

Deirdre served as the HSBA Appellate Section Chair during 2021-2023.

Deirdre is admitted to practice before all Hawai‘i state courts; the federal District Court for the District of Hawaiʻi; the Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals; and the United States Supreme Court.

Deirdre has published two recent articles on appellate procedure in the Hawaii Bar Journal:

• Appellate Procedural Traps: Fifteen Confusing or Counter-Intuitive Procedural Rules for Civil Appeals in the State Appellate Courts and How to Avoid Them, August 2023

• Pro Tips for Writing Appellate Motions and Briefs in the State Appellate Courts, August 2024

attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Hilo, HI
attorneys.bio:
ROBERT MARX: HAWAII PERSONAL INJURY AND AUTO ACCIDENT ATTORNEY ON THE BIG ISLAND

The last thing anyone wants is to be reduced to a number on some law firm’s client list. Everyone wants to feel that careful attention is being paid to his or her individual case. Robert Marx understands his personal injury clients' needs and, as their trusted attorney, endeavors to satisfy them. On the Big Island of Hawaii, cases could range from an auto accident that requires the attention of an attorney. Both are treated with equal regard at The Law Office of Robert Marx, where we believe that how you play the game is just as important as winning.

ROBERT MARX, PERSONAL INJURY ATTORNEY – BACKGROUND INFORMATION

A fixture in Big Island legal circles for more than 42 years, Robert Marx has helped countless personal injury victims over the course of his career. Robert’s family came to Hawaii in 1921. In fact, some of his older clients still remember his grandparents, Bascilio and Maxima Belin. This good-humored and hard-working immigrant family put down Hawaii roots in Kalihi.

Two generations later, Robert graduated from Oregon State University in 1971 with a bachelor’s degree in political science. Before receiving his Doctor of Jurisprudence at Lewis and Clark College in 1979, Robert Marx served three terms as an elected member of the Oregon House of Representatives. While in office, he was responsible for supporting and passing important legislation in the area of nursing home care. In 1977, he was voted Senior Citizen Advocate of the Year by the American Association of Retired People’s and Retired Educator’s Legislative Committee. The following year, he served as an appointed member of the Governor’s Commission on Aging.

Robert began practicing law in Hilo in 1980. He now has an office in Hilo, catering to people from every part of the Big Island. For over two decades, Robert and his talented staff have fought to help residents of Hawaii in the settlement and advocacy of auto accident and personal injury claims. Attorney Robert Marx has steadfastly served the Big Island, devoting his entire career to the place he is proud to call home.

If you live in Hawaii and have been involved in an auto accident or other personal injury situation, contact attorney Robert Marx to schedule a consultation at one of our Big Island offices.

attorneys.bio:
Jennifer Ching-Agena is admitted to both the Hawai'i State Bar Association and the Washington State Bar Association. She is a Family Law attorney experienced in divorce, post-divorce, custody, child support, and temporary restraining orders. Ms. Ching-Agena is a graduate of Creighton University School of Law.

Ms. Ching-Agena attended Creighton University College of Business Administration and graduated cum laude where she earned her B.S.B.A and majored in International Business and Social Entrepreneurship. She then continued her time in the Midwest and attended Creighton University School of Law where she graduated with her JD. During her time in Law School, she volunteered at Iowa Legal Aid.

Ms. Ching-Agena then moved to Washington State where she volunteered at a Legal Aid society and worked for various Family Law firms and an Insurance Defense firm. The majority of her time spent in Washington State was focused on litigating Family Law matters such as divorce, child custody, child support, and temporary protective orders.

Upon moving back home to Hawai'i, Ms. Ching-Agena joined Greg Ryan & Associates where she zealously advocates for her clients.

attorneys.name: Michael J. O'Malley
attorneys.firm_name: Goodsill Anderson Quinn & Stifel A Limited Liability Law Partnership LLP
attorneys.practice_type: Tax Lawyers in Honolulu, HI
attorneys.bio:
Michael J. O’Malley represents for-profit and nonprofit clients in their initial organization and structuring, business dealings, M&A transactions, infrastructure, capital and other financings, regulatory compliance, tax planning and proceedings before tax authorities, and also addresses issues of corporate governance and fiduciary duty.

His work includes:

Tax Planning and Disputes: Represents domestic and foreign businesses, organizations and individuals in planning and structuring their transactions, activities and affairs to lower their overall federal, state and local tax burden and minimize their related risk and exposure; obtaining private letter rulings and determination letters from the IRS and Hawai‘i Tax Departments in connection with tax-free reorganizations, “qualified high technology business” applications and credits, and other tax incentive and structuring matters; and settling disputes with federal, state and local tax authorities.

Healthcare: Advises healthcare organizations, providers and insurance companies on compliance, regulatory, tax, corporate and transactional matters.

Mergers and Acquisitions: Represents buyers and sellers of businesses, including stock purchases, asset sales and mergers. Representative transactions include stock and asset acquisitions and changes in control of public and private corporations, including a real estate company, a developer, a newspaper, a gas company, an equipment company, hospitals, health care organizations and medical practices, a construction company, and various retail businesses.

Corporate Organization and Governance: Organizes for-profit and non-profit corporations, prepares charter documents establishing complex capital structures, stock transfer restrictions, buy-sell and first refusal rights and supermajority voting requirements. Advises corporate directors concerning fiduciary duties, conflicts of interest and compliance with the Hawaii Business Corporation Act and other federal and state laws and regulations.

Corporate Finance: Advises clients with respect to their various financing transactions, including infrastructures and other project financings and capital, leasing and other financings.

Mike served as Editor-in-Chief of the Harvard Journal on Legislation and was a teaching assistant at Harvard Law School. Following graduation, he practiced with a Wall Street firm in New York City for four years, then returned home to Hawai‘i and joined Goodsill Anderson Quinn & Stifel A Limited Liability Law Partnership LLP, where he became a Counsel in the firm’s corporate and tax groups. He rejoined the firm in 2008, following a fifteen-year hiatus during which he was a partner at another Hawai‘i law firm, then worked for nine years as a director with PricewaterhouseCoopers and its successor in Hawai‘i. Since 1986, he has authored or co-authored the Hawai‘i chapter of the ABA Deskbook on Sales and Use Tax. He is a frequent speaker at seminars on tax, corporate and other legal topics. Since 2019 Co-Authored Real Property Tax Deskbook.

Mr. Okamoto grew up in Waipahu, where he attended public school through high school. He received his undergraduate degree in Political Science from the University of Hawai‘i at Mānoa in 2001, and his Juris Doctor from the University of Hawai‘i William S. Richardson School of Law in 2005. Following his graduation from law school, Mr. Okamoto served as law clerk to Circuit Court Judge Steven S. Alm (Ret.).

After devoting five years to attending to family matters, Mr. Okamoto began his career in 2013 as a solo practitioner specializing in criminal defense, personal injury, and family law.

In 2021, Mr. Okamoto decided to focus exclusively on family law and joined the law firm of Kleintop & Luria, LLP. While at Kleintop & Luria, he specialized in complex divorce litigation.

Mr. Okamoto joined Greg Ryan and Associates in 2025 as a skilled practitioner in all aspects of family law. He is a zealous advocate and takes pride in providing effective and efficient representation to all clients. He excels at balancing a client’s needs with legal strategy to achieve the best possible outcome for his clients.

Mr. Okamoto is also committed to giving back to the community, and serves as a volunteer with the Kapolei Access to Justice Room.

Mr. Okamoto is licensed to practice law in the State of Hawai‘i, the United States District Court for the District of Hawai‘i, and the United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit. Mr. Okamoto is also a member of the Family Law Section of the Hawai‘i State Bar Association.

attorneys.name: Raymond K. Okada
attorneys.firm_name: Goodsill Anderson Quinn & Stifel A Limited Liability Law Partnership LLP
attorneys.practice_type: Trust and Estate Litigation and Controversy Lawyers in Honolulu, HI
attorneys.bio:
Raymond Okada has a practice encompassing all aspects of estate planning, wills, trusts and probate. His practice includes planning and administering estates, as well as resolving will and trust disputes and tax controversies. He has served clients from diverse backgrounds, family situations and wealth. He has earned an AV® rating by Martindale-Hubbell Law Directory, election to the prestigious American College of Trust and Estates Counsel (Chair, Fiduciary Litigation Committee, past Hawaii State Chair), and a listing in Best Lawyers in America. Examples of his work include:

Basic Estate Planning: Prepared hundreds of "typical" estate planning documents, such as wills, revocable living trusts, durable powers of attorney (for both asset management and health care), living wills, and insurance trusts.

Advanced Estate Planning: Prepared documents to implement more sophisticated planning techniques such as generation skipping trusts, family limited partnerships, qualified personal residence trusts, charitable remainder trusts, grantor retained income trusts, qualified domestic trusts, "defective" irrevocable trusts, buy-sell agreements for corporations and partnerships and reorganizations of corporations to achieve estate planning goals.

Probate & Trust Administration: Counseled fiduciaries (personal representatives of probate estates and trustees of trusts) on proper administration, including fiduciary accounting of principal and income, income taxation of trusts and estates, tax compliance, prudent investor decisions and fiduciary responsibility and liability.

Post Mortem Planning: Counseled family, fiduciary and accountants with respect to planning after death, such as the use of qualified disclaimers, the tax consequences of allocating assets between various trusts or beneficiaries and making tax elections.

Litigation and Disputes: Prosecuted as well as defended will contests and trust contests in suits to set aside the document because of lack of capacity, undue influence or fraud. Prosecuted as well as defended fiduciaries in suits for breach of fiduciary duty. Handled estate tax audits, primarily on issues of valuation of assets, including discounts.

Family Business Planning: Counseled businesses owned by families on forming entities, dissolving entities, and business succession planning, including entity structuring, techniques for transferring ownership and control, and creating trusts and/or entities to hold transferred entity interests.

Ray is a frequent lecturer for both professional and lay groups, including the Hawaii State Bar Association (HSBA), the Hawaii Society of Certified Public Accounts (HSCPA), the National Business Institute (NBI), Hawaii Tax Institute and the University of Hawai‘i Emeritus Program. He is the author of How to Use the Generation Skipping Tax Exemption, financial and estate planning seminar (HSBA, 1992), Income Taxation of Trusts and Estates (NBI, 1995), Drafting for Generation Skipping Transfer Tax Planning (financial and estate planning seminar, 1994), Serving as Trustee can be Risky Business (Pacific Business News, 2000), and Shedding Light on Sunset: Estate Planning under the 2001 Tax Act (HSCPA seminar, 2001). Ray has also served as adjunct professor of Wills and Trusts at the William S. Richardson School of Law at the University of Hawai‘i.

OUTSIDE THE OFFICE

Ray is a sought-after speaker for groups like the Hawai‘i State Bar Association (HSBA), Hawai‘i Society of Certified Public Accounts (HSCPA), National Business Institute (NBI), Hawai‘i Tax Institute and the University of Hawai‘i Emeritus Program.
